# N3-B2-A contract and compatibility evidence

This gate adds exactly the eleven approved new contract/evidence/test/documentation files. No existing source is edited. Native commands, effects, proof v2, version-2 codec/capability execution, application v2 integration and rich editor reads remain unimplemented. Production remains the Legacy Task Service. Stop for user review before N3-B2-B.

The completed sequential baseline preserved 1,610 exact files and full dirty Git status (601 entries with `--untracked-files=all`; this is distinct from grouped status counts). Current plugin data contains 178 History rows and six checks. Six predecessor seals, B1's 4,278 internal files, its inventory checksum and 25 current reviewed outputs verified before source additions. No live native pointer/generation/fence/lock artifacts were present. Mutable execution/builds are guarded to OS Temp.

The full verified B1 ZIP SHA256 is `8beab2df463b49aa9f4e93606235fd436cb75358a8a35a280ad6b8aed7eabbb0`. The previous response duplicated its valid value with an unnecessary transcription note; the implementation's initial description that it was shortened was mistaken and corrected. No seal was substituted or historical evidence rewritten.

`ItacanTaskCore/atomic-task/CONTRACT.md` and `contracts.d.ts` freeze the proposed hybrid Save/rich initializer, complete revisions/digests/bindings, Step dispositions, deterministic effect ordering, truthful genuine/initial completion provenance, effect-backed E2 suppression and F2 proof v2. Creation-time capability, no existing-root upgrade, all-write/replay fallback fencing, prepared-occurrence reopening and deferred editor reads reflect the user's selections. There is no runtime entry point or new command implementation.

The 654-file source graph contains actual reviewed baseline bytes, origins and SHA256 values, including the pre-B2 private reader and unchanged older-reader fixtures. Its digest binds 107 unique vectors. Vectors explicitly distinguish proposed behavior, current executable observations and unresolved limits. Passing manifest accounting does not establish implementation of proposed behavior.

The two new test files execute existing native construction, strict N1-C structure/content, the shared completion helper in an explicitly unpublished detached experiment, initial checked/null-time state, unchanged checked state, retirement/retained History, actual imported reopening/recompletion and recurrence A/E1/B then A/E2 successor reuse. They also verify current core/writer/application rejection of proposed commands, coherent N2/F2 v1 provenance refusal and preserved causal unknown.

Actual domain validation accepts a deliberately changed stored command name when its otherwise old receipt relationship is retained, while its strict result fields reject an unknown atomicTask field. This adversarial specimen is not a valid future Save receipt. It demonstrates that command names alone are insufficient and supports the reviewed terminal capability barrier.

Twelve new child executions run actual frozen schema1/B1/B2/pre-B2 private readers on explicitly labelled proposed-format goldens. The pre-B2 cases cover logical schemas 1/4, manifest/generation versions and unknown capability, with a checksum-valid, decodable older revision-zero recovery pointer present. Old readers refuse with UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA; tested files remain unchanged. These are actual reader executions, not mocks or new codec output. All children are awaited. A introduces no persistence boundary, new crash worker or claim that the proposed all-write barrier is implemented.

The new declarations include positive complete command/effect/intent/proof/editor-contract examples and negative misuse cases. They prove the proposal remains outside the actual core Command union and that v2 proof cannot be supplied as a v1 port without negotiation.

Initial development failures are retained: BOM-bearing JSON fixture decoding and synchronous command rejection were initially handled with the wrong test APIs. Corrected only new fixtures/assertions; no historical test, source hash, expected failure or policy was weakened. Inspection-only Python output also encountered Windows default-codepage decoding/printing errors; those failures establish no verification result. Accepted runs and raw failures are recorded separately.

Three reporting-only failed attempts are also retained with their commands, raw output and nonzero exits. The first assumed B1's dead-lock filename for N2 evidence; the second did not distinguish a post-release null lock; the third incorrectly treated a later reconstruction lease in an archived raw-root snapshot as the terminated child's lease. The corrected report validates exact original PID/host/token/bytes where a lock existed, and explicitly verifies the two recorded close-after-release stages. A later copied lease has a different PID and is not removed or relabelled. No reporting failure established passing acceptance or changed an original test.

Final executed inventories, source/protected comparisons, build results, archived interruption evidence and seal are recorded below after completion. No partial reporting result establishes acceptance. Claims are limited to executed existing behavior, proposed-format reader refusal and declaration compatibility; they exclude atomic Save execution, new proof/codec support, new enabled-root recovery, cross-store coordination, power loss/cloud rollback, hostile writers, distributed uniqueness and complete-directory rollback detection.

## Final acceptance

36/36 new tests passed with zero failures, cancellations or skips. The new TypeScript 6.0.3 runner reports zero diagnostics. All 38 exact saved inventories passed: 23 behavioral inventories and 15 existing declaration runners, plus the new declaration check (16 total). No new exclusions. All 138 E1 frozen assertions and 137 current behavioral checks retain their established distinction.

The four original actual-reader assertions passed unchanged:

- ok 118 - Actual frozen schema1 reader rejects E2 manifest without fallback
- ok 119 - Actual frozen schema1 reader rejects E2 generation without fallback
- ok 120 - Actual frozen B1 reader rejects E2 manifest without fallback
- ok 122 - Actual frozen B2 reader rejects E2 manifest without fallback

Twelve additional actual-reader executions against proposed goldens passed. Exact golden files and their hashes are retained separately from real new-codec output, which does not exist. Thirty-two retained existing parent-termination records reverified child death: 30 retained locks match PID/host/token and exact bytes/hash; two close-after-release cases correctly have no lock; they are inherited reruns, not new B2 interruption scenarios. Other original fault-exit/crash evidence remains in raw saved-suite logs.

No existing protected file differs from the fresh baseline at the recorded comparison.

All twelve staged assets match byte-for-byte; main/Atlas remain 168/24 factories, one Legacy construction and no native/atomic startup. Installed assets remain unchanged. No live native artifacts were found outside backups.

Exactly eleven approved new files, zero existing-source edits. Proposed native commands/proof v2/storage capability and B integration remain unimplemented.

Private sealed package: `System/Backups/itacan-n3b2a-20261019-ma0955ti`.
